title: Land acknowledgement adopted at first meeting of new Council
subtitle: Deputy Mayor rotation, strategic planning, sports betting revenue, interim tax levy, snowmobile trail agreement and 2023 meeting schedule.
overview: Council's first meeting of the new term adopted a land acknowledgement for Centre Wellington, with a wording change to refer to the area now known as the Township of Centre Wellington {{vote:m1}}. It will be used at Council and public meetings, official meetings with Indigenous Nations, and formal events. Staff described it as a first step toward truth and reconciliation.

Council also set up how it will work this term. It appointed members to external boards and committees and approved a rotating Deputy Mayor, with the order drawn by lottery {{vote:m3}}. It started a new strategic planning process for 2023 to 2026 {{vote:m4}}. It adopted the 2023 meeting schedule {{vote:m2}}.

On money, Council approved an amendment to the Ontario Lottery & Gaming agreement so the Township receives a share of sports betting revenue {{vote:m5}}. It passed the 2023 interim tax levy, which changes the non-residential and multi-residential due dates to match residential ones {{vote:m7}}, and a temporary borrowing by-law {{vote:m6}}. Council also awarded the Elora wastewater plant lighting contract {{vote:m8}}, approved an agreement with the local snowmobile club {{vote:m10}}, and adopted the Victoria Park Senior Centre's revised constitution {{vote:m9}}.

decisions.detail: Council received the report and approved the land acknowledgement as amended, for use at Council and public meetings and at official Indigenous meetings and formal events.
Council appointed members to external organizations and committees and authorized a by-law for a rotating Deputy Mayor for the term, repealing By-law 2021-09.
Council approved starting a new strategic planning process for the 2023 to 2026 term.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign an amendment giving the Township a share of sports betting proceeds from the Elora gaming facility.
Council passed the interim levy by-law, with first-quarter due dates for non-residential and multi-residential properties moved to match residential ones.
Council awarded the light replacement project to Motion Electrical Contracting Ltd. at $24,031.75 excluding HST.
Council authorized an agreement with the Fergus Elora Belwood Snowmobile Club to operate, inspect and maintain snowmobile trails on Township property.
Council adopted the 2023 Council and committee meeting schedule and directed that it be posted on the Township website.

debate: On the land acknowledgement, one councillor asked whether the reading could be shared among Council members to keep it from becoming routine. Another suggested the wording "in the communities now known as" the Township, since the Township is a relatively new legal entity, and the presenter agreed.
Staff said the acknowledgement would be used at more significant meetings rather than every committee meeting, so it stays meaningful and is not recited by rote.

On the sports betting amendment, one councillor asked whether adding a betting option affects community well-being. Staff pointed to material from the OLG saying a portion of its funds goes toward customer health and well-being. Staff also said the OLG revenue allocation policy will be reviewed in the 2023 budget process.

On the snowmobile agreement, councillors asked about insurance and liability. Staff said club membership requires proof of insurance, the OPP also patrols the trails, and the Township faces no added risk. One councillor asked for a follow-up report on safer routes to the trails.

On timing of advisory committees, a councillor asked whether committees would lose anything while strategic planning is under way. Staff said they are aware of committee needs and some committees continue under legislation.
